title: Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM)

exam.scoring: Pass/fail against the PMI target across all domains

content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the PMI CAPM examination content outline (four official domains and weightings). Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A company's team is creating a one-time, unique mobile payment application for a client while a separate group handles day-to-day server maintenance and support. Which statement best distinguishes the project from the operations work?
options: The project is temporary and produces a unique deliverable, while operations are ongoing and repetitive
The project is continuous and the operations team produces a unique product
The project repeats the same routine daily and operations delivers a one-off result
Both the project and the operations are permanent efforts with identical outputs
items.explanation: A project is defined as a temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result, while operations are ongoing, repetitive activities that sustain the business. The other options reverse these definitions.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: An organization coordinates a group of related projects, such as a warehouse automation build and the supporting logistics system, under one umbrella to obtain benefits that would not be available if the projects were managed separately. How should these projects be characterized?
options: As a project management office, because it assigns project managers
As a program, because the projects are related and managed jointly to achieve coordinated benefits
As a portfolio, because each project is unrelated and independently budgeted
As operations, because the work repeats in every release
items.explanation: A program is a group of related projects managed together to deliver coordinated benefits not available individually. A portfolio is a broader collection of work aligned to strategy, and long-running routines are operations, not a program.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A company groups all its projects, programs, and routine support work together so leadership can review, prioritize, and select the mix that best advances strategic objectives. What does this collection of work represent?
options: A project life cycle
A program
A portfolio
A work breakdown structure
items.explanation: A portfolio is the collection of projects, programs, and other work grouped to meet strategic business objectives. The other choices are narrower: a program is related projects only, not routine work.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A team is building a one-off regulatory reporting engine that will be retired after a single use by the client. Which two core characteristics identify this effort as a project?
options: It is ongoing and produces the same output every cycle
It has no defined start date and no defined end date
It only involves routine operational tasks with no deliverable
It is temporary in nature and creates a unique product, service, or result
items.explanation: A project has a beginning and an end and creates a unique deliverable. Operations are ongoing and repeatable, and every project has defined start and completion dates.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: Early in a construction project, the project manager knows the overall scope but refines details such as finishing materials and fixtures only as design work progresses. Which concept does this behavior best illustrate?
options: Progressive elaboration, where the product definition is developed incrementally as more information becomes available
Immediate finalization of all requirements before planning begins
Decomposition of the project into a permanent operations process
Iterative scheduling of a fixed timetable
items.explanation: Progressive elaboration means product and project details become clearer and more precise as the work proceeds. The other choices describe fixed, upfront delivery or ongoing operations rather than iterative detailing.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A newly appointed project manager has been given the authority to apply organizational resources to project activities and to lead the team. Which document formally authorizes this authority?
options: The project management plan
The project charter
The work breakdown structure
The stakeholder register
items.explanation: The project charter is issued by the sponsor and formally authorizes the project, naming the project manager and transferring authority to apply resources. The plan, WBS, and register come after initiation.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: During initiation, an executive approves a new system rollout and formally issues the document that authorizes the project to begin and provides the project manager with authority. Who most commonly issues this document?
options: The procurement officer
The business analyst
The project sponsor
The functional manager
items.explanation: The sponsor is the person or group that provides resources and support and issues the project charter. The business analyst, functional manager, and procurement officer have other roles.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project hits an impasse when an external vendor refuses a delivery schedule that the project team negotiated. The project manager needs someone with organizational influence to resolve the conflict and secure the delivery commitment. Whose support should the project manager seek?
options: The quality assurance lead
The configuration manager
The procurement clerk
The project sponsor
items.explanation: The sponsor champions the project, removes escalated obstacles, and uses executive influence to resolve disputes that exceed the project manager's authority. The other listed roles do not hold that authority.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager plans team activities and assigns work daily, while an executive approves the budget, resolves high-level issues, and champions the project to the board. Which statement about these stakeholders is correct?
options: The executive is the sponsor, who supports the project and provides resources, while the project manager runs day-to-day work
The project manager is the sponsor because the project manager controls the schedule
The executive is the project manager because the executive owns the budget
Neither role has a defined responsibility in project governance
items.explanation: The sponsor provides resources, funding, and executive support, while the project manager manages day-to-day planning and execution. The other options confuse the two distinct roles.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A generic project life cycle is used to structure a new initiative. In which order do the four phases of this generic life cycle typically occur?
options: Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Controlling
Start the project, organize and prepare, carry out the work, and end the project
Identify, Study, Design, Operate
Requirements, Design, Testing, Deployment
items.explanation: The generic project life cycle comprises starting the project, organizing and preparing, carrying out the work, and ending the project. Process groups and SDLC phases are different structures.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager wants to structure all project work into the standard five grouping categories that apply regardless of the industry or development approach. Which set does the project manager use?
options: Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver, Decommission
Feasibility, Approval, Construction, Handover, Warranty
Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Controlling, Closing
Concept, Design, Build, Test, Support
items.explanation: The five process groups are Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Controlling, and Closing. The other lists are phase naming conventions specific to particular life cycles or industries.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: During execution, a project manager notices the team is completing features more slowly than planned and compares progress against the baseline to evaluate what is happening and decide whether corrective action is needed. Which process group is the project manager primarily applying?
options: Closing
Initiating
Planning
Monitoring and Controlling
items.explanation: Monitoring and Controlling tracks, reviews, and regulates progress and performance against the plan, triggering corrective or preventive actions. It is not initiating, planning, or closing work.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project has delivered its final release, the client has formally accepted every deliverable, and the team has handed project documentation to the operations group. Which remaining activities belong to the Closing process group?
options: Releasing team resources, finalizing accounts, and capturing lessons learned
Drafting the project charter and identifying stakeholders
Estimating activity durations and sequencing tasks
Executing quality assurance checks on every deliverable
items.explanation: Closing involves releasing resources, closing contracts and financial accounts, archiving information, and capturing lessons learned. Chartering and estimating belong to earlier process groups.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project completed on time and within budget, yet six months later the business reports the new system did not deliver the anticipated savings. Which perspective best explains this outcome?
options: On-time delivery guarantees that business value was created
Delivering outputs on schedule is only part of success; the project must also achieve the intended benefits and value
A project is successful only if it finishes within budget, regardless of realized value
Benefits are the sole responsibility of the operations team after the project closes
items.explanation: Project success is measured not only by deliverable outputs but by the benefits and value realized from them. Finishing on schedule without achieving benefits is incomplete success.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: While managing a legacy migration, the project manager must balance the classic triple constraint with its extended partners. Which set of factors is most commonly described as the competing constraints of a project?
options: Requirements, design, and testing deliverable phases
Vendors, contracts, and purchase orders
Scope, schedule, and cost, extended by quality, resources, and risk
People, process, and technology only
items.explanation: The classic triple constraint is scope, schedule, and cost, frequently extended to include quality, resource, and risk considerations that the project manager must balance.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: During planning, the project manager records that a critical vendor will likely deliver hardware within three weeks, although this is believed to be true without any binding confirmation. How should this statement be classified in the project documents?
options: As a deliverable, because hardware is a project output
As a risk response, because it mitigates supply risk
As a constraint, because it limits the schedule
As an assumption, because it is taken as true without proof for planning purposes
items.explanation: An assumption is a factor believed to be true but not yet verified, used to allow planning to proceed. A constraint is a hard limitation, and the other choices are unrelated concepts.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: At project initiation, the project manager lists individuals from a regulator, the engineering team, the customers, and the main supplier so that their interests can be considered throughout the project. What should this list be called?
options: The stakeholder identification output, capturing anyone who can affect or be affected by the project
The project steering committee charter
The supplier evaluation shortlist
The project management team roster
items.explanation: Stakeholders are individuals, groups, or organizations who may affect, be affected by, or perceive themselves to be affected by the project. The other lists describe narrower operational groups.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager categorizes stakeholders by their power to influence the project and their interest in its outcome, then selects engagement strategies accordingly. Which grouping approach is being used?
options: The WBS dictionary
The power/interest grid from stakeholder analysis
The RACI responsibility chart
The earned value management baseline
items.explanation: The power/interest grid classifies stakeholders by their authority level and their interest in the project to target communication and engagement. RACI assigns responsibilities, and EVM and the WBS serve other purposes.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: During stakeholder analysis, a project manager groups stakeholders using three attributes: power to influence, urgency of their claims, and the legitimacy of their involvement. Which stakeholder classification model is the project manager applying?
options: The earned value technique
The risk breakdown structure
The salience model
The critical path method
items.explanation: The salience model classifies stakeholders by combinations of power, urgency, and legitimacy to prioritize attention. The other options address scheduling, performance measurement, or risk categorization.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: After identification, a project manager creates a document capturing each stakeholder's name, position, expectations, influence level, and engagement requirements so strategies can be tailored to each one. Which document is being produced?
options: The procurement management plan
The risk register
The cost baseline
The stakeholder register
items.explanation: The stakeholder register records identification and assessment information about each stakeholder, such as expectations, influence, and engagement needs. The other documents serve unrelated management areas.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager compares each stakeholder's current level of engagement with the desired level and then plans targeted actions, such as increased briefings, to close the gap. Which tool is the project manager most likely relying on?
options: The stakeholder engagement assessment matrix
The critical path diagram
The lessons learned register
The resource calendar
items.explanation: The stakeholder engagement assessment matrix plots current versus desired engagement levels (such as unaware, resistant, neutral, supportive, leading) so the team can plan actions to reach the target state.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A steering committee member with strong influence resists the project because of a past failed initiative. The project manager plans one-on-one sessions to understand the concerns and earn support. Which best-practice principle is the project manager following?
options: Limit engagement to stakeholders who already approve the project
Actively engage all stakeholders from the start to build and maintain their support
Ignore resistant stakeholders until full delivery is achieved
Escalate every resistant stakeholder directly to termination
items.explanation: Managing engagement requires actively involving stakeholders throughout the project to gain support and reduce resistance. Ignoring or terminating stakeholders undermines project governance.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: During the Initiating group, a sponsor asks the project manager to produce the document that states the business need, provides a high-level description of the product, and formally authorizes work to begin. Which document should be produced first?
options: The sprint backlog
The detailed work breakdown structure
The project charter
The procurement contract
items.explanation: The project charter is developed in Initiating and links the project to strategy while authorizing the project manager. Detailed planning documents such as the WBS come later, and contracts are procurement outputs.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: Before launching a new subscription platform, leadership wants a documented financial and strategic justification, including projected costs, benefits, and alignment with corporate goals, to decide whether to proceed. What should be developed?
options: A stakeholder register
A resource histogram
A change request log
A business case
items.explanation: The business case documents the business need and financial justification for the project and informs project selection and approval. The other documents are created during or after initiation.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager consolidates the scope, schedule, and cost baselines with subsidiary plans for quality, risk, and communication into one authoritative reference for executing the project. What is the project manager producing?
options: The project management plan
The project charter
The issues log
The stakeholder register
items.explanation: The project management plan integrates all subsidiary management plans and baselines and defines how the project is executed, monitored, and controlled. The charter authorizes, the issues log tracks problems, and the register lists stakeholders.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A change request that would extend the schedule must be evaluated for impacts across quality, cost, and risk before any decision is made. Which process formalizes the review, approval, and incorporation of such changes?
options: Monitor Stakeholder Engagement
Perform Integrated Change Control
Direct and Manage Project Work
Acquire Resources
items.explanation: Perform Integrated Change Control reviews all change requests, assesses cross-functional impacts, approves or rejects changes, and manages baseline changes. The others are execution, resource, or engagement processes.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: During execution, a project manager ensures data from daily tasks is converted into usable reporting that the team can act on. Which sequence correctly matches the project management information flow?
options: Work performance information, then work performance data, then work performance reports
Work performance reports, then work performance data, then work performance information
Work performance data, then work performance information, then work performance reports
Work performance reports, then work performance information, then work performance data
items.explanation: Raw measurements from performing activities are work performance data; analyses of the data against baselines produce work performance information; and consolidated information becomes work performance reports.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: Late in a project, a team member discovers a technique that could accelerate deployment and wants future teams to benefit from it. Which practice directly supports transferring this knowledge?
options: Burning all project documentation to protect confidentiality
Deleting the lessons learned register before closing
Withholding the technique until after the project is archived
Capturing the insight as a lesson learned and recording it in the lessons learned register throughout the project
items.explanation: Managing project knowledge means capturing lessons learned continuously so insights can be used during the project and by future projects, rather than losing them at the end.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager must know which organizational body provides common standards, templates, and governance procedures that all projects are expected to follow. Which body is described?
options: The project management office (PMO)
The project steering committee
The change control board
The procurement team
items.explanation: A PMO standardizes governance, processes, templates, and metrics across projects. A steering committee governs decisions, a CCB approves changes, and the procurement team manages vendors.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: Within a project team, the project manager delegates specialized estimating to three experts while a fourth person handles project records and reporting. How are these individuals collectively best described within the team structure?
options: They are members of the project management office governance body
They are part of the project management team, a subset that performs project management activities
They are the formal steering committee of the project
They are external auditors with no project responsibility
items.explanation: The project management team is the subset of the project team that directly performs management activities such as planning, reporting, and controlling. The other options name different governance or support structures.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager wants a matrix that assigns a single accountable owner and clear roles for every work package, spanning responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed levels. Which tool should the project manager create?
options: A communication channel count
A control chart
A RACI chart
A risk register
items.explanation: A RACI matrix maps work packages to team members as Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed, clarifying roles and reducing ambiguity. The other tools address risk, communications, or quality control.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A sponsor asks a project manager for one tool to systematically identify the underlying cause of repeated late deliveries rather than treating individual symptoms. Which technique should the project manager choose first?
options: A budget reconciliation to relocate funds
A stakeholder classification grid
A procurement make-or-buy analysis
A fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram to trace potential causes of the delay
items.explanation: Root cause analysis using a cause-and-effect (fishbone) diagram structures potential causes of a recurring problem so the team can address the source. The other options do not diagnose causes.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: The project manager must choose between two software vendors by scoring each against weighted criteria such as cost, capability, and support. Which decision-making technique is most appropriate?
options: Multi-criteria decision analysis using weighted scoring
Random selection to avoid bias
A coin toss supervised by the vendor teams
Choosing the vendor with the lowest estimated price only
items.explanation: Multi-criteria decision analysis scores and weights multiple criteria so choices reflect the project's priorities rather than a single factor or arbitrary selection.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A new project manager must lead a team scattered across four time zones using asynchronous tools and periodic joint sessions. Which practice best supports a high-performing virtual team?
options: Avoiding documentation because the team is remote
Defining clear communication protocols, expectations, and accountability up front
Requiring every member to relocate to a single office
Scheduling meetings only for the project manager's local time zone
items.explanation: Virtual teams thrive when expectations, communication channels, and working hours are explicit and mutual, complemented by occasional co-location or face-to-face sessions. Forcing relocation ignores the virtual model.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager is deciding how decisions will be escalated and who has the authority to approve changes that affect the cost baseline. Which structure or framework should define these rules?
options: The stakeholder engagement matrix
The activity resource estimation
The project governance framework
The earned value report
items.explanation: Project governance defines the framework of rules, procedures, and authority levels for decision-making and escalation. The other tools address performance, engagement, or resource estimation.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: An executive questions whether a project should be funded at all, given competing demands. The project manager points to a governing decision made above the project level that selected and prioritized this work against others. Which concept is the project manager referring to?
options: The physical resource assignment plan
The project closure report
The team building activity schedule
Organizational project management that aligns projects to corporate strategy
items.explanation: Organizational project management and portfolio selection ensure projects are chosen and prioritized because they align with strategic objectives. The other options concern execution-level details.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A junior team member asks what distinguishes a milestone from a regular deliverable in the project schedule. Which explanation is correct?
options: A milestone is a significant point or event in the project with zero duration, used to mark progress
A milestone is any task that requires more than one person
A milestone is a budget reserve held for risks
A milestone is a document delivered at project closure only
items.explanation: Milestones are zero-duration events that mark significant points such as phase completions or key approvals. They have no work or duration, unlike tasks and deliverables.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: Stakeholders begin adding small, unapproved enhancements to the work scope as the project proceeds, so the project manager must decide how to handle this behavior. Which PMI best practice should the project manager apply?
options: Tell the team to ignore stakeholder requests entirely
Control the scope by documenting the additions and routing them through change control before approval
Accept every addition silently to keep stakeholders satisfied
Work overtime to include all additions without updating the baseline
items.explanation: Unofficial scope additions constitute scope creep. The PMI approach is to capture proposed changes and evaluate them through integrated change control so scope remains baselined and controlled.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: During planning, the project manager involves stakeholders to clarify requirements, then uses that input to detail the project plan incrementally until it is comprehensive. Which phrase best describes this planning behavior?
options: Deferring all planning until after execution begins
Replacing planning with daily standup meetings
Developing the plan iteratively through progressive elaboration
Committing to a single upfront plan that can never change
items.explanation: Project planning is iterative: the plan is progressively elaborated as requirements, assumptions, and constraints become clearer. A single rigid upfront plan and abandoning planning are both anti-patterns.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A new stakeholder joins a project midway through execution. Besides welcoming the stakeholder, what should the project manager do with relation to the stakeholder register?
options: Freeze the register because it was finalized during initiating
Remove the stakeholder unless they were identified at project start
Ask the stakeholder to create the register themselves
Update the register so the stakeholder's influence and engagement needs are assessed and planned
items.explanation: Stakeholders can appear at any time, so identification and analysis continue throughout the project and the register is updated accordingly. A fixed register wrongly ignores new stakeholders.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project team prepares status reports and distributes them so leadership can make decisions, but one powerful stakeholder reacts with surprise at recent cost increases. Which principle should the team follow going forward?
options: Proactively share timely, accurate information with the right stakeholders at the right time
Stop reporting cost data to all stakeholders
Report only favorable progress to avoid conflict
Wait until project end to share any financial information
items.explanation: Effective communication means engaging the right stakeholders with the right information at the right time. Withholding or smoothing unfavorable data undermines transparency and decision-making.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: Before work begins, project leadership confirms the funds needed for the work packages planned in the near term. Who most commonly provides this funding authority and confirms the availability of resources at initiation?
options: The external audit team, who observes progress
The sponsor, who provides resources and support for the project
The project coordinator, who maintains the schedule
The business analyst, who documents needs
items.explanation: Sponsors secure funding approval and provide resources, whereas coordinators, analysts, and auditors have supporting or oversight roles rather than funding authority.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager must distinguish the project manager's authority from that of the sponsors and other leaders. Which primary source formally delegates authority to the project manager?
options: The vendor contract signed with the first supplier
The project schedule baseline
The project charter issued and approved by the sponsor
The personal approval of the most senior team member
items.explanation: The charter is the source of the project manager's authority to apply organizational resources and make decisions. Vendor contracts and the schedule baseline do not grant that authority.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager must quickly determine whether a newly discovered government filing requirement will affect how the project is staffed, funded, and reported. Which category does this regulation and its templates belong to?
options: Radically new software deliverables of the project
Team building exercises for the project staff
Permanent output of the project management office
Enterprise environmental factors and organizational process assets that influence the project
items.explanation: Legislation, market conditions, and infrastructure are enterprise environmental factors, while policies, templates, and lessons learned are organizational process assets; both influence how the project is run.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project team completes planning and the project manager schedules a session to align the team and key stakeholders around expectations, the plan, and how work will proceed before execution begins. What is this session called?
options: The project kickoff meeting
The daily standup meeting
The project retrospective
The bidder conference
items.explanation: A kickoff meeting communicates project objectives, roles, and the plan to the team and key stakeholders, aligning everyone before execution. Standups are daily scrums, and retrospectives occur later.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A product is developed through multiple phases of a large initiative, and leadership is deciding the highest-level structure that governs the product's own full lifespan from conception through retirement. Which term applies?
options: The communication matrix of the delivery team
The product life cycle, which extends beyond a single project
The work breakdown structure of one release
The resource calendar for the current phase
items.explanation: The product life cycle spans the product's entire existence, while a project life cycle covers a single project that may deliver only a part of that product. The other options are project-level artifacts.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project has received its final deliverables, but the project manager wants to formally confirm that each deliverable was accepted and the project can close. Which step best supports this closure?
options: Escalating all deliverables to the operations team without review
Declaring closure solely based on the budget remaining positive
Obtaining formal acceptance sign-off from the customer or sponsor before closing
Deleting the completion records to simplify archival
items.explanation: Closing includes securing formal acceptance of deliverables and confirming obligations are complete before activities such as archiving and releasing the team. Sign-off protects both customer and seller.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager must model how a major deliverable depends on another task finishing first. Which scheduling concept defines this mandatory finish-to-start relationship between two activities?
options: A reserve allocation for schedule risk
A stakeholder sensitivity rating
An earned value index calculation
A dependency relationship in the schedule network
items.explanation: Precedence relationships sequence activities; a finish-to-start dependency means the successor cannot start until the predecessor finishes. Reserves, ratings, and EVM are unrelated to sequencing.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: During the very early definition of a project, the team has only a rough idea that the deliverable must reduce order-processing time, with all specific outcomes to be refined later. Which characterization is most accurate?
options: The scope is high-level now and will be progressively detailed through planning
The scope is fully frozen and cannot be detailed further
The scope must be defined by the operations team at closure
The scope is irrelevant until execution begins
items.explanation: Early project scope is intentionally high level and becomes progressively more detailed as analysis and planning proceed, consistent with progressive elaboration. The other options contradict this principle.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager decides to lead the team by delegating decisions to members who have the expertise, while still being accountable for the overall result. Which leadership stance does this reflect?
options: A leadership vacuum where no one is accountable
Servant and facilitating leadership that empowers the team while maintaining accountability
Abandoning accountability to the team entirely
Authoritarian control of every detailed task
items.explanation: Modern PMI guidance favors leaders who facilitate, serve, and enable the team while remaining accountable for outcomes. Dismissing accountability or micromanaging every task are not recommended.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager meets a stakeholder who demands a favor in exchange for supporting an upcoming budget approval. The project manager declines and discloses the offer to leadership. Which PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct value is the project manager upholding?
options: Respect, by quietly accepting the demand
Responsibility, by withholding the incident from the team
Fairness, by avoiding favoritism and disclosing a potential conflict of interest
Honesty, by promising the stakeholder anything to gain approval
items.explanation: Fairness requires avoiding favoritism and disclosing conflicts of interest rather than trading decisions for personal advantage. Secretly accepting or hiding the demand would violate the Code.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A status report shows the project is over budget, and the project manager must deliver the news to the steering committee. Which action aligns with the PMI Code of Ethics?
options: Adjust the numbers so the variance appears smaller
Delay reporting until the budget improves
Present only the favorable financial metrics
Report the accurate figures truthfully, even though the news is unfavorable
items.explanation: Honesty requires accurate and truthful communication, including reporting unfavorable results. Manipulating, delaying, or cherry-picking data misrepresents project performance.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: During a planning workshop, a demanding stakeholder repeatedly interrupts others and dismisses their concerns. The project manager listens to each viewpoint and ensures every participant is heard before decisions are made. Which Code of Ethics value is being practiced?
options: Respect, by listening to others' points of view and treating them fairly
Honesty, by avoiding the topic of disagreement
Fairness, by agreeing with the loudest participant only
Responsibility, by ending the meeting early
items.explanation: Respect in the PMI Code includes listening to others' viewpoints and cooperating with them. Candor and full participation, not deferring to the loudest voice, characterize respectful conduct.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
items.stem: A project manager witnesses a colleague intentionally omitting required testing from a delivered release and incorrectly certifying it as complete. What does the PMI Code of Ethics require in this situation?
options: Congratulating the colleague for saving time
Reporting the violation to relevant authorities in a timely manner
Silently accepting the act to protect the colleague
Altering the test records to match the certification
items.explanation: Responsibility under the Code includes reporting illegal or unethical conduct to appropriate parties when it is observed. Falsifying records or staying silent compounds the violation.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts

items.stem: A client has detailed, stable requirements, a fixed budget, and an immovable regulatory deadline for a compliance reporting system. Which approach is most appropriate for this project?
options: An incremental approach that delivers incomplete reporting to production
A hybrid approach with no defined scope or schedule
A predictive, plan-based approach with a defined sequence of phases and minimal late change
An adaptive approach that discovers requirements during execution
items.explanation: Predictive approaches fit projects with clear, stable requirements and controlled changes, allowing detailed upfront planning of scope, schedule, and cost against a fixed deadline.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: In a traditional waterfall project, the design phase must finish completely before development begins, and customers review outcomes only at phase gates. What drawback is most likely with this structure?
options: Requirements can change freely without re-planning
The team can deliver value in the first week
Risk is eliminated by avoiding changes
Late changes are expensive because earlier phases are already complete
items.explanation: Sequential phases lock in outputs early, so discovering new requirements or defects late forces rework of completed phases, making change expensive. Change is not free or risk-free in this model.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: After defining scope, the project manager breaks deliverables into smaller components all the way down to work packages that can be scheduled, estimated, and assigned. Which tool is being created?
options: The work breakdown structure (WBS)
The critical path method diagram
The communications matrix
The stakeholder power grid
items.explanation: The WBS hierarchically decomposes project deliverables into work packages for estimating, scheduling, and assigning ownership. The other tools address scheduling, communications, or stakeholders.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: For each work package in the WBS, a project manager records the deliverable description, acceptance criteria, responsible organization, and cost account so teams execute consistently. Which artifact captures this detail?
options: The resource histogram
The WBS dictionary
The risk breakdown structure
The change log
items.explanation: The WBS dictionary accompanies the WBS with detailed information for each element, including scope, deliverables, milestones, and acceptance criteria. The other documents serve different purposes.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A project has performance requirements that can be measured, such as transaction speed, and support requirements that describe quality features, such as usability. How are these best documented for tracing to deliverables?
options: As vendor questionnaires with no link to the WBS
As a single verbal agreement retained only in meeting minutes
As types of requirements linked in a traceability matrix from source to deliverable and test
As confidential personnel records unrelated to scope
items.explanation: Requirements are categorized and recorded in a requirements traceability matrix that links each requirement to its source, WBS deliverable, and validation activity. The other choices fail to formalize them.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: The team has completed the deliverable defined in the WBS, and a project manager coordinates with the customer to review and formally accept it. Which scope process is being performed?
options: Control Scope, which only involves change requests
Define Scope, which creates the scope statement
Collect Requirements, which gathers stakeholder needs
Validate Scope, obtaining formal acceptance of the completed deliverables
items.explanation: Validate Scope reviews deliverables with the customer or sponsor and obtains formal acceptance. Collect and Define Scope occur earlier; Control Scope manages changing scope against the baseline.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: During execution, a project manager detects that the amount of completed work is not matching the scope planned in the baseline and investigates the variances to decide whether corrective action is required. Which process is the project manager performing?
options: Control Scope, which monitors scope status and manages baseline changes
Direct and Manage Project Work, which assigns daily tasks
Plan Scope Management, which sets policies
Close Project, which archives the scope statement
items.explanation: Control Scope uses variance analysis against the scope baseline to detect deviations and drives corrective action or change requests. The other processes have different timing and outputs.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: In a schedule network, a database migration task must be completely finished before the application cutover can begin. Which dependency type describes this relationship?
options: Start-to-finish
Finish-to-start
Start-to-start
Finish-to-finish
items.explanation: A finish-to-start dependency requires the predecessor to complete before the successor starts, the most common relationship in precedence diagrams. The other types allow overlapping or different sequences.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: To compress the schedule, a project manager considers beginning installation work a few days before design documentation is fully archived. Which scheduling technique adds time ahead of the successor?
options: A finish-to-start lag on the critical path only
An increase in total float
A lead, which accelerates the successor by overlapping work
A lag, which inserts a delay between activities
items.explanation: A lead allows a successor activity to start before the predecessor finishes, overlapping and compressing the schedule; a lag delays the successor. Leads and lags are adjustments to dependencies.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A project network shows multiple paths through the schedule, and the project manager needs the sequence that determines the earliest project completion and has no schedule flexibility. Which path is this?
options: The path with the most number of milestones
The shortest path in the network
The path with the greatest cost
The critical path, the longest path with the least (typically zero) total float
items.explanation: The critical path is the longest duration path through the network; any delay on it delays the project, giving it zero or minimal total float. Other paths are non-critical.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A non-critical task in the schedule can slip by several days without affecting the project finish date. What is this flexibility called, and what does it measure?
options: Total float, the amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project end date
Free float, which applies only to procurement contracts
Contingency reserve, which is budget rather than time
Duration compression, which is a scheduling action
items.explanation: Total float is how long an activity can be delayed from its early start without postponing project completion. Free float concerns the successor start, and reserves are cost or time buffers, not activity slack.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A project manager needs a fast, rough duration estimate for a new office build using the actual durations of a very similar completed office build. Which estimating technique is being applied?
options: Parametric estimating, applying a productivity rate times quantity
Analogous estimating, using historical data from similar activities
Bottom-up estimating, summing every detailed work package
Three-point estimating, averaging three duration scenarios
items.explanation: Analogous estimating uses historical durations from similar prior activities as a basis, making it fast but less accurate. Bottom-up, parametric, and three-point estimates use different calculation bases.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: An estimator records a most likely duration of 20 days with an optimistic duration of 14 days and a pessimistic duration of 26 days for a task. Using the PERT (beta) three-point formula of (optimistic + 4 x most likely + pessimistic) divided by 6, what is the expected duration?
options: 18 days
24 days
20 days
22 days
items.explanation: The PERT expected duration is (14 + 4 x 20 + 26) / 6 = 120 / 6 = 20 days. Weighing the most likely value four times differentiates PERT from a simple average.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A schedule has two parallel paths: path one through tasks A, B, and C totals 15 days, and path two through tasks X, Y, and Z totals 18 days. What is the duration of the critical path?
options: 15 days
33 days
3 days
18 days
items.explanation: The critical path is the longest duration path, so 18 days determines the project duration. It is not the sum of both paths or the shorter path.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A project manager tracks progress using earned value management. Which pairing of the three core metrics with their definitions is correct?
options: Planned value is approved budget for planned work, earned value is budget for completed work, and actual cost is money spent
Earned value is money spent, planned value is cost variance, and actual cost is the schedule variance
Planned value is total profit, earned value is customer debt, and actual cost is the budget baseline
Planned value is the estimate at completion, earned value is the project charter, and actual cost is sunk cost
items.explanation: EVM compares the value of completed work (EV) against the budgeted value of planned work (PV) and the money actually spent (AC). The other options misassign meanings to the metrics.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: At month six, a project shows PV of 30,000, EV of 25,000, and AC of 22,000 in monetary units. Using the formulas CV equals EV minus AC and SV equals EV minus PV, what is the project's cost and schedule status?
options: Behind schedule and over budget, because AC is lower than PV
Behind schedule and under budget, because SV is negative and CV is positive
Ahead of schedule and over budget, because EV is lower than PV
On schedule and on budget, because variances are equal
items.explanation: CV = 25,000 - 22,000 = +3,000 (positive, under budget) and SV = 25,000 - 30,000 = -5,000 (negative, behind schedule). The signs of each variance reveal the true status.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A project's earned value is 40,000, planned value is 50,000, and actual cost is 44,000 in monetary units. Which statement correctly interprets the cost performance index (CPI = EV / AC) and schedule performance index (SPI = EV / PV)?
options: CPI is 0.80 and SPI is 0.91, so the project is under budget and on schedule
CPI is 1.00 and SPI is 1.00, so the project is on plan
CPI is 0.91 and SPI is 0.80, so the project is over budget and behind schedule
CPI is 1.10 and SPI is 1.25, so the project is under budget and ahead of schedule
items.explanation: CPI = 40,000 / 44,000 = 0.91 and SPI = 40,000 / 50,000 = 0.80. Indexes below 1.0 indicate cost overrun and schedule slippage respectively.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A project manager sets aside an amount in the budget to cover known risks that are included in the risk register, and a separate amount for unspecified, unknown risks. How are these two amounts correctly described?
options: Management reserve for known risks and contingency reserve for unknown-unknowns
Both amounts are cost baseline increases for scope expansion
Neither amount belongs in the total budget
Contingency reserve for known risks and management reserve for unknown-unknowns
items.explanation: Contingency reserve addresses identified risks and is part of the baseline; management reserve addresses unplanned, unknown work and is held outside the cost baseline until approved.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A manufacturer compares the cost of prevention and appraisal activities with the cost of defects, rework, and warranty claims to justify a quality investment. Which quality concept is the manufacturer applying?
options: Cost of quality, balancing conformance and nonconformance costs
Earned value analysis of schedule performance
Procurement make-or-buy analysis
Stakeholder power assessment
items.explanation: Cost of quality weighs conformance costs (prevention and appraisal) against nonconformance costs (rework, scrap, warranty), showing that investing in quality can reduce overall cost. The other tools are unrelated.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A quality engineer monitors a production process and plots sample measurements over time with control limits, so that points outside the limits signal a process that needs investigation. Which quality tool is being used?
options: A fishbone diagram
A control chart
A Pareto diagram
An affinity diagram
items.explanation: Control charts track a process over time and reveal whether it is stable and in control; points outside control limits trigger investigation. Pareto, affinity, and fishbone diagrams serve other analyses.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A project manager must ensure quality is built into the process by auditing that planned and followed activities actually meet quality requirements. Which project quality management process focuses on this audit-based assurance role?
options: Plan Quality Management, which identifies quality requirements
Close Project, which archives quality records
Manage Quality, which audits and improves the quality process itself
Control Quality, which inspects completed deliverables
items.explanation: Manage Quality (assurance) audits process compliance and improves workflows so deliverables meet quality requirements, whereas Control Quality verifies the deliverables themselves against acceptance criteria.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: After identifying dozens of project risks, a risk manager first scores each risk by its probability and impact on a simple scale to rank them, deferring detailed simulation until later. Which analysis is being performed initially?
options: Quantitative risk analysis, using Monte Carlo simulation
Risk response planning, assigning owners to all risks
Procurement risk evaluation, quoting insurance premiums
Qualitative risk analysis, prioritizing risks by probability and impact
items.explanation: Qualitative risk analysis rapidly prioritizes risks by assessed probability and impact using ratings; quantitative analysis numerically analyzes effects (e.g., via simulation) afterward when warranted.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A construction firm decides to purchase an insurance policy so the insurance company absorbs financial loss if a crane causes damage on site. Which risk response strategy is being used?
options: Transfer, shifting the impact of the risk to a third party
Avoid, eliminating the activity that creates the risk
Mitigate, reducing the probability or impact of the risk
Accept, acknowledging and assuming the risk
items.explanation: Transfer shifts the financial consequences of a risk to another party, typically through insurance or contracts. Avoid eliminates the cause, mitigate reduces it, and accept retains it.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A project manager identifies an opportunity to receive an early-bird discount if a supplier order is placed before the end of the month. Which strategy should the project manager use to increase the chance of seizing this opportunity?
options: Accept, ignoring the discount window
Exploit, acting to ensure the opportunity happens
Avoid, eliminating the activity entirely
Transfer, moving the opportunity to a competitor
items.explanation: Exploit is the positive risk strategy that seeks to make the opportunity certain by securing it, such as placing the order early. Enhance and share are other opportunity responses, and accept retains it.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: For a well-understood, fixed set of deliverables, a buyer and seller agree on a set total price that will not change unless the scope changes. Which contract type has transferred most cost risk to the seller?
options: Time and materials, where the buyer pays hourly rates plus costs
Fixed-price with award fee, which always increases the price
Fixed-price, where the seller bears the cost overrun risk
Cost-reimbursable, where the buyer pays all allowable costs
items.explanation: In fixed-price contracts the seller carries the cost risk because the price is set for a defined scope. Cost-reimbursable and time-and-materials contracts place more cost risk on the buyer.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A project communications manager counts the pairwise interactions needed on a project with 12 stakeholders, including the project manager. Using the formula n times (n minus 1) divided by 2, how many communication channels exist?
items.explanation: With n = 12, the channel count is 12 x 11 / 2 = 66. Many people multiply without dividing, but the formula counts unique pairwise links, not ordered pairs.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies

items.stem: A product owner expects the market to shift frequently and admits that many customer needs are undiscovered. The team must deliver working capability early and adjust often. Which development approach is most appropriate?
options: An adaptive approach with iterative delivery and continuous feedback
A predictive waterfall with all requirements fixed upfront
A single-phase approach that waits for perfect specifications
An approach that fixes scope but changes the deadline weekly
items.explanation: Uncertain, changing requirements favor adaptive (agile) approaches that iterate rapidly and incorporate feedback each cycle. Predictive planning presumes stable requirements the others lack.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A team starts each two-week cycle by selecting the highest-priority work, builds and tests it together, and at the end reviews usable results with the customer. How is this cycle best described?
options: A compliance review with no working output
Iterative and incremental delivery of working functionality
A single predictive release at project completion
Continuous day-to-day operations support
items.explanation: Iterative delivery repeats development cycles to refine the product, and incremental delivery adds finished capability each cycle, so the customer sees usable results regularly.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: An agile team relies on making work visible, frequently inspecting results and adjusting practices in response. Which three pillars of empirical process control does this reflect?
options: Authority, responsibility, and accountability
Design, develop, and deploy
Transparency, inspection, and adaptation
Planning, executing, and closing
items.explanation: Scrum's empirical control uses transparency of work and information, frequent inspection of artifacts and progress, and adaptation of process and product. The other sets describe unrelated categories.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: In a Scrum team, one member is accountable for maximizing the value of the product by managing and ordering the product backlog while representing stakeholder needs to the team. Which role is this?
options: The scrum master
The delivery manager
The change control board
The product owner
items.explanation: The product owner owns the product backlog, orders it for value, and communicates stakeholder and customer needs. The scrum master coaches the process, and a CCB is a governance body.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: During a sprint, the team is blocked by a purchasing approval that must be obtained to continue a key work item. The coach for the agile process removes the blocker and ensures the team's working environment is effective. Which role is acting?
options: The scrum master, who facilitates and removes impediments
The product owner, who writes user stories
The executive sponsor, who codes the software
The quality tester, who approves purchases
items.explanation: The scrum master serves the team by removing impediments, facilitating events, and coaching agile practices. The product owner manages value, and sponsors and testers have different duties.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A Scrum development team has all the skills needed to design, build, test, integrate, and deliver a feature without depending on people outside the team, and members choose how to accomplish their own sprint work. Which two attributes does this team demonstrate?
options: Co-located and vendor-supplied
Self-organizing and cross-functional
Externally directed and functionally siloed
Hierarchically managed and specialized
items.explanation: Scrum teams are self-organizing in choosing how to perform their work and cross-functional in possessing every needed skill to create a done increment. Siloed or externally directed teams violate the model.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A Scrum team consistently uses four-week periods to produce a product increment, keeping the period length fixed so they can learn to forecast delivery. What is the correct term and purpose for this fixed period?
options: A release train, which deploys every day
A milestone, which has zero duration
A sprint, a timeboxed iteration during which a usable increment is created
A backlog refinement, an endless planning session
items.explanation: Sprints are timeboxed iterations, typically one month or less, producing a done increment each time; a fixed length improves forecasting. The other options are not sprint equivalents.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: At the start of an iteration, the team collaborates to choose which backlog items will be worked on and to define the goal that focuses the sprint's work. Which event is taking place?
options: The daily scrum
The sprint retrospective
The product backlog review
Sprint planning
items.explanation: Sprint planning selects the scope for the sprint from the backlog and defines a sprint goal. The daily scrum tracks progress, and retrospectives improve the process.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: Each working day, an agile team meets for a short standup in which each member states what was done, what is planned next, and any obstacles, so the team can inspect progress toward the sprint goal. Which ceremony is described?
options: The daily scrum
The sprint review
The sprint retrospective
The milestone gate
items.explanation: The daily scrum is a 15-minute timeboxed event for inspecting progress toward the sprint goal and adapting the plan. Sprint review inspects the increment, and the retro examines the process.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: At the end of a sprint, the team demonstrates the completed increment to stakeholders, who give feedback that the team uses to reorder the backlog. Which event is this?
options: The project chartering session
The sprint review
The daily scrum
The sprint retrospective
items.explanation: The sprint review inspects the increment with stakeholders and uses their feedback to adapt the product backlog. The retrospective, by contrast, reviews team process, and the daily scrum is much shorter.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: After a chaotic sprint, the team reflects on how they worked together, what went well, what blocked them, and how to improve their process in the next sprint. Which event is the team performing?
options: The stakeholder analysis workshop
The procurement negotiation
The sprint retrospective
The sprint planning session
items.explanation: The sprint retrospective focuses on the team's process and collaboration so it can improve next sprint. Sprint planning selects work, and stakeholder analysis is a separate activity.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: An agile team maintains a single, ordered list of all desired work and ideas for the product, refined and re-prioritized as new information appears, and owned by the product owner. Which artifact is this?
options: The sprint backlog
The risk register
The requirements traceability matrix
The product backlog
items.explanation: The product backlog is the emerging, ordered list of everything the product needs, owned by the product owner; the sprint backlog is only the subset selected for one sprint.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: During sprint planning, the team agrees on the selected backlog items plus a plan for how to deliver them, which the team then updates throughout the sprint as they learn more. What is this combination called?
options: The sprint backlog
The product roadmap
The definition of done
The product vision
items.explanation: The sprint backlog contains the sprint scope, selected from the product backlog, plus the team's plan to create the increment, and it is adjusted as the sprint proceeds.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: An agile team agrees on the shared, verifiable conditions that a product increment must meet to be considered complete and potentially releasable, including tests passed and documentation done. Which artifact formalizes this agreement?
options: The velocity target
The definition of done
The product roadmap
The cost baseline
items.explanation: The definition of done is the team's agreed set of completion criteria ensuring each increment is usable and potentially shippable. Roadmaps show releases, and velocity measures output rate.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A delivery team limits how many items may be in progress at once, pulls new work only as capacity becomes free, and manages work continuously rather than in timeboxed iterations. Which method is the team using?
options: Waterfall with phase gates
eXtreme Programming with pair programming only
Kanban with work-in-progress limits and pull-based flow
Scrum with fixed sprints and role ceremonies
items.explanation: Kanban governs a continuous, pull-based flow by limiting work in progress so items complete before new work is pulled. Scrum uses timeboxed sprints, and XP describes distinct engineering practices.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A manager wants a visual chart showing the flow of work states on a Kanban board over time and where bottlenecks are forming. Which chart should the team maintain?
options: A sprint burndown chart
A Pareto chart
A control chart for defects
A cumulative flow diagram
items.explanation: A cumulative flow diagram displays counts of work items in each Kanban state over time, exposing bottlenecks and flow stability. Burn down charts track remaining work, not multi-state flow.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A development team writes a test before implementing a feature, authors code in pairs, and integrates continuously so defects are found early. Which agile methodology emphasizes these engineering practices?
options: eXtreme Programming (XP)
Kanban
Scrum
Lean startup
items.explanation: XP emphasizes engineering practices such as test-driven development, pair programming, continuous integration, and small releases. Kanban focuses on flow, and Scrum defines roles and events rather than coding practices.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: An agile team writes short descriptions of functionality from a user's perspective in the format of a role, a goal, and a benefit so each item is testable and valuable. What technique for expressing requirements is this?
options: Data dictionaries
User stories
Use case diagrams
Business process maps
items.explanation: User stories express requirements as concise role-goal-benefit statements that can be sized and tested. Use cases and process maps are different, more formal representation techniques.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: An agile team completes 24 story points in the current sprint after delivering 20 and 22 in prior sprints, and the product owner uses this pattern to forecast future capacity. Which measure is the team using?
options: Earned value management with CPI
Cumulative float across the portfolio
Velocity, the amount of work completed per iteration
Throughput on the critical path
items.explanation: Velocity is the useful output completed per iteration, averaged over sprints to forecast capacity. Throughput, EVM, and float measure different schedule or value concepts.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: Before each sprint, the team and product owner inspect and split larger backlog items into smaller ones with details and estimates so items are ready to be picked up. Which activity is being performed?
options: Definition of done creation
Sprint retrospective
Release train assembly
Backlog refinement
items.explanation: Backlog refinement keeps the product backlog detailed, estimated, and ordered so items are ready for sprint planning. The definition of done is static criteria, and retrospectives review process.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: An agile team sizes a new feature by comparing it against a small, well-understood baseline story and then votes together on the estimate until the team converges. Which estimation approach is the team using?
options: Relative estimation with planning poker
Analogous estimating from a corporate database
Bottom-up estimating of every task hour
Parametric estimating with productivity rates
items.explanation: Planning poker uses relative comparison against a reference story with team voting to converge on a consensus estimate, a hallmark of agile estimating. The others are traditional estimating techniques.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A scrum master coaches the team to solve its own problems, shields it from interference, and asks questions rather than giving orders to build the team's capability. Which leadership style is being demonstrated?
options: Laissez-faire leadership with no support
Servant leadership, prioritizing team growth and autonomy
Command and control management of every task
Micromanagement of individual developer activity
items.explanation: Servant leaders put the team's needs first, build capability, and remove impediments so the team can self-organize. The other styles either control too tightly or abandon the team.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A project must satisfy a fixed regulatory submission window while still discovering detailed product features with the users. Which approach best serves this combination of constraints?
options: A purely adaptive approach that ignores the fixed deadline
Discontinuing all planning to save time
A hybrid approach that timeboxes iterations for feature discovery while preserving the fixed compliance milestone
A purely predictive approach with no customer feedback
items.explanation: Hybrid models combine predictive structure for fixed, must-meet requirements and deadlines with adaptive, iterative work where requirements are uncertain, balancing both sets of constraints.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: An agile team is spread across multiple countries and time zones. Which adaptation most supports effective agile collaboration in this virtual structure?
options: Withholding daily status so team members work in isolation
Requiring every member to work identical fixed hours overnight
Abandoning the product backlog because the team is remote
Using shared visual boards and overlapping communication windows to keep work transparent
items.explanation: Virtual agile teams rely on visible artifacts and deliberate communication rhythms to remain transparent and aligned across time zones. Isolating work or discarding the backlog breaks empirical control.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A developer is juggling five unfinished tasks at once and constantly switching contexts. The Kanban team decides each person may work on only one item at a time and must finish it before pulling new work. What is the team limiting?
options: Work in progress, to reduce multitasking and shorten cycle time
The sprint length, to increase ceremony
The definition of done, to lower quality
The team size, to cut communication channels
items.explanation: Limiting work in progress is the core Kanban mechanism: fewer open tasks reduce context switching, expose bottlenecks, and shorten the time for each item to complete.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A scrum team notices that meetings drag on and planning never seems to end. The team decides to give every event a fixed maximum duration. Which agile concept formalizes this practice?
