options: Cumulative flow, charting board states
Timeboxing, capping the duration of an activity to focus effort
Velocity tracking, measuring output per sprint
Definition of done, setting quality criteria
items.explanation: Timeboxing assigns a maximum fixed duration to events so they stay focused and predictable, forcing prioritization. The other concepts measure output or define completion rather than bounding time.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A startup wants to learn what customers really value before building a full product, so it ships the smallest useful feature set to gather real feedback early. Which concept does this practice illustrate?
options: Building the entire product in one unplanned release
Hiding features from customers until launch
Delivering a minimum viable product early to test assumptions and get feedback
Deferring all feedback until full project completion
items.explanation: An MVP delivers the least functionality that provides value and tests key assumptions so teams learn and redirect early. Delaying feedback until the end is the opposite of this practice.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: An agile team values working with customers directly and adapting to changes over rigid processes and documentation-heavy handoffs. Which set of agile values is the team honoring?
options: Contracts and detailed documentation above all else
Following a fixed plan with no adaptation
Tools and processes over people and results
Individuals and interactions, working software, customer collaboration, and responding to change
items.explanation: The Agile Manifesto values individuals and interactions, working software, customer collaboration, and responding to change over the heavier alternatives while still respecting those alternatives.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: A product owner releases a small, valuable capability to real customers after every iteration and uses the resulting usage data to reorder what the team builds next. Which principle does this cadence of frequent release and feedback follow?
options: Deliver working product frequently so stakeholders can steer the product with real feedback
Deliver everything only at the very end of the program
Ignore customer usage data and follow the original plan exactly
Release features in reverse priority order
items.explanation: Agile principles call for delivering working increments frequently and using stakeholder feedback to steer subsequent work toward optimal value instead of waiting until final delivery.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: An agile team wants defects to surface as soon as code changes occur rather than months later. Which combination of practices best supports early and continuous quality assurance?
options: Removing verification to meet the sprint deadline
Test-driven development with continuous integration and automated testing
Postponing all testing to a final phase gate
Documenting defects only after customer reports them
items.explanation: TDD writes tests before code, and continuous integration with automated tests validates every change, catching defects at the moment they are introduced instead of at the end.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Agile Frameworks/Methodologies

items.stem: On a project, one practitioner focuses on understanding and defining the business problem and the requirements that solve it, while another focuses on planning, executing, and controlling the work to deliver a solution. How are these roles correctly described?
options: Both roles are identical and interchangeable in all activities
The business analyst owns the schedule and the project manager owns the requirements
The business analyst defines needs and requirements while the project manager delivers the solution within constraints
The project manager defines requirements and the business analyst controls the budget
items.explanation: Business analysts define stakeholder needs and requirements and evaluate solutions, while project managers plan, execute, and control the project that delivers the solution. The roles are complementary but distinct.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst starts a new engagement by confirming what the business wants to achieve, who is affected, and whether the initiative is feasible before any requirements are detailed. Which activity describes this first step?
options: Running the sprint retrospective to review the last iteration
Closing the project and archiving documents
Negotiating the fixed-price contract with the seller
Conducting a needs assessment to determine the business need and how it aligns with strategy
items.explanation: Needs assessment analyzes the business problem or opportunity and its alignment with strategy before requirements work begins. Retrospectives, closure, and contracting are later or separate activities.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst compares the current state of an order process with the desired future state and identifies the gaps that a new system must close. Which technique best supports this comparison?
options: Gap analysis comparing current and desired business states
Control chart analysis for process stability
Critical path scheduling of system deployment
Work breakdown structure decomposition
items.explanation: Gap analysis examines the differences between the current and desired states to define what the solution must achieve. Control charts, CPM, and the WBS serve quality, scheduling, and decomposition purposes.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: Before committing resources, leadership asks whether the proposed system can realistically be built with available technology, skills, budget, and time. Which study should the business analyst conduct?
options: A vendor auction for the lowest bid
A feasibility study to assess whether the solution can be delivered
A stakeholder power grid to rank executives
A procedure to record lessons learned
items.explanation: A feasibility study evaluates technical, economic, and organizational viability before approval. Power grids, lessons learned, and procurement auctions address different concerns.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst must articulate why spending on a new analytics platform is justified, including the expected financial and nonfinancial returns. Where should this justification be documented?
options: In the configuration management audit
In the resource histogram
In the business case, which captures expected benefits and value
In the sprint retrospective outcome
items.explanation: The business case records the justification, expected benefits, and value of an initiative. Retrospectives, configuration audits, and resource histograms capture other kinds of information.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst needs input from dozens of geographically dispersed customers to understand their purchasing preferences. Which stakeholder communication technique is most effective for gathering this kind of broad input?
options: A private face-to-face interview with one executive only
A lunch meeting with the development team
A password reset for the customer forum
A structured survey or questionnaire distributed to the full audience
items.explanation: Surveys and questionnaires efficiently collect standardized input from large, dispersed audiences. Interviews suit depth with few stakeholders rather than broad reach across many people.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst must explore a complex workflow in depth with a small group of specialists who can challenge each other's ideas to refine requirements. Which elicitation technique is most appropriate?
options: A facilitated workshop with the relevant subject matter experts
A broadcast email asking for requirements
A random opinion poll of the general public
A review of procurement invoices
items.explanation: Facilitated workshops bring key stakeholders together to define and cross-check requirements collaboratively and quickly. Mass emails and polls lack the interaction needed for complex workflows.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst sits beside customer service agents and records exactly how they process returns so the future system matches reality. Which elicitation technique is being used?
options: Prototyping a final user interface
Observation, capturing real-world behavior in context
Brainstorming in a creative session
Questionnaire distribution to managers
items.explanation: Observation records how work is actually performed in its environment, revealing details participants may not disclose in interviews. Brainstorming, surveys, and prototyping are different techniques.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: During requirement prioritization, the team labels a feature as essential for launch, another as important if time allows, and a third as nice to have. Which prioritization scheme is the team applying?
options: An earned value calculation of budget
A risk likelihood rating scale
MoSCoW, categorizing requirements as must, should, could, and will not have
A critical path analysis of schedule tasks
items.explanation: MoSCoW prioritization groups requirements into must have, should have, could have, and will not have so scope decisions are explicit. The other options address scheduling, cost, or risk.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst separates requirements that describe what the system must do, such as calculating tax, from those that describe performance or usability, such as responding within two seconds. Which categorization is correct?
options: Nonfunctional requirements describe behavior and functional requirements describe quality
Both categories describe only user interface colors
Neither category applies to software systems
Functional requirements describe behavior, while nonfunctional requirements describe qualities and constraints
items.explanation: Functional requirements specify what the product does, whereas nonfunctional requirements specify performance, security, usability, and other quality attributes and constraints.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst reviews existing procedures, process maps, and legacy reports to understand how the current system works before defining change. Which elicitation technique is this?
options: Document analysis to understand the as-is state
A timeboxed sprint planning session
A contract negotiation with suppliers
A random sampling of user passwords
items.explanation: Document analysis mines existing materials to understand current processes and identify relevant requirements efficiently. Sprint planning, negotiation, and sampling do other work.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst draws a diagram showing the new system in the center and the external actors interacting with it around the boundary, clarifying what is inside and outside the system's scope. Which modeling technique is this?
options: A fishbone diagram
A context diagram
A Pareto chart
A control chart
items.explanation: A context diagram defines the system boundary and its interactions with external entities, supporting scope definition. Pareto, control, and fishbone diagrams are quality or cause-analysis tools.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst models the interactions between an end user and the system to define the sequence of steps needed to reach a goal such as placing an order. Which representation is most suited to this?
options: A cost performance index spreadsheet
A stakeholder power grid
Use cases that describe the actor-system interactions and flows
A resource histogram of staff utilization
items.explanation: Use cases capture the interactions between actors and a system to achieve a goal, defining triggers, flows, and outcomes. The other artifacts address staffing, cost, or stakeholder analysis.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst creates a diagram tracing how data moves, transforms, and is stored across the business functions when an order is processed. Which modeling tool is the analyst using?
options: A burndown chart
A communications matrix
A risk breakdown structure
A data flow diagram
items.explanation: Data flow diagrams map how information flows and transforms through processes and stores, clarifying data movement for requirements. The other tools track progress, communications, or risks.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: To confirm screen layout expectations, a business analyst builds a simple, nonfunctional mock-up of the future interface for users to react to before final development. Which elicitation and analysis technique is being applied?
options: Prototyping, using a working model to refine and validate requirements
Document mining of legacy source code
A vendor evaluation scorecard
A Monte Carlo cost simulation
items.explanation: Prototypes are lightweight models that users interact with to clarify and validate interface requirements early, reducing rework. The other techniques do not produce an interactive representation.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst must ensure every documented requirement can be followed from its source through design and testing to the final delivered component. Which artifact makes this tracking possible?
options: A stakeholder engagement matrix
A requirements traceability matrix
A velocity burndown chart
A procurement statement of work
items.explanation: A requirements traceability matrix links each requirement to its origin, associated deliverables, and verification activities, supporting change and coverage analysis. The other documents lack that linkage.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: An agile team defines for a user story the specific, verifiable conditions that must hold for the story to be accepted, such as a generated receipt and an emailed confirmation. What is the team defining?
options: The cost baseline
The project governance rules
Acceptance criteria for the story
The communication management plan
items.explanation: Acceptance criteria are the measurable conditions a requirement must satisfy for acceptance. Communication plans, cost baselines, and governance frameworks address different project aspects.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst checks whether a stated requirement was recorded correctly and is complete, then later checks whether the built solution actually satisfies that stated requirement. Which pair of concepts describes these two checks in order?
options: Validation, confirming requirements are well formed, then verification, confirming the solution meets them
Both checks review the project budget variance
Both checks occur only after project closure
Verification, confirming requirements are well formed, then validation, confirming the solution meets them
items.explanation: Requirements verification ensures requirements statements are complete and correct, while solution validation evaluates whether the delivered solution satisfies the requirements and achieves intended value.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A stakeholder proposes a new requirement that would noticeably expand the solution. Before accepting it, the analyst assesses its impact on cost, schedule, and other requirements and routes it through formal approval. Which discipline does this reflect?
options: Requirements change control, evaluating and approving requirement changes deliberately
Silent acceptance of every new proposal
Deleting the requirements baseline entirely
Postponing the decision to project closure
items.explanation: Requirements management includes change control: proposed changes are analyzed for impact and approved or rejected against the baselined requirements. Silently accepting or deleting baselines undermines control.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: In an agile project, the business analyst performs activities that closely resemble the work of a product owner by detailing, clarifying, and ordering requirements in the backlog. How should this role adaptation be described?
options: Agile projects have no requirements of any kind
Business analysis responsibilities adapt to the methodology, here focusing on backlog management and story definition
Business analysis is eliminated entirely in agile projects
Business analysts never interact with stakeholders in agile projects
items.explanation: Business analysis exists in every methodology but changes shape: in agile, analysts feed, refine, and prioritize the backlog and define stories rather than producing upfront requirement documents.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: An executive wants a visual overview of how planned features and capabilities will be delivered across upcoming releases over time. Which artifact should the business analyst produce and maintain?
options: A monthly invoice reconciliation
A change control board agenda
A product roadmap showing the planned evolution of the product across releases
A detailed resource histogram
items.explanation: A product roadmap communicates the high-level sequence of planned features and releases over time, aligning stakeholders on direction. The other artifacts cover staffing, finance, or governance.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A team holds a roadmap that shows release themes while the product backlog contains individual prioritized stories. Which relationship between these artifacts is correct?
options: The backlog replaces the roadmap and no planning view is needed
The roadmap lists hourly resource assignments
The backlog is a financial ledger of the project
The roadmap provides the release-level view, and the backlog elaborates the concrete work items
items.explanation: The product roadmap communicates planned releases and themes at a high level, while the product backlog contains the prioritized, detailed work that implements those themes in each cycle.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: When building a product roadmap, the analyst must decide which features belong in the first release and which in later releases. Which set of factors should drive that partitioning?
options: Business value, dependencies, risk, and stakeholder priorities across releases
The alphabetical order of feature names
The number of developers on vacation
Office floor allocations for each team
items.explanation: Release planning sequences features by value, dependencies, risk, and stakeholder priority so each release delivers coherent, valuable capability. Arbitrary orderings ignore these drivers.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A program plans a launch for a flagship feature in release one, a supporting set of enhancements for release two, and only backlog cleanup for release three. What activity shaped this plan?
options: Server capacity monitoring
Release planning that assigns features to releases based on value and dependencies
Earned value reporting of past releases
Procurement bid evaluation
items.explanation: Release planning groups requirements into releases so each release delivers meaningful value on a viable schedule. The other options measure past performance or manage vendors and infrastructure.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: In a hybrid project, one person owns the prioritized backlog and objective setting while a scrum master coaches the team each iteration. How is the backlog owner most accurately characterized in this setup?
options: Serving as the configuration auditor
Replacing the need for any stakeholder communication
Fulfilling the product owner's responsibilities, including requirement priority and stakeholder representation
Acting as the project sponsor who funds the effort
items.explanation: The product owner role owns backlog ordering and works as the voice of the customer, even when a business analyst assists with requirement details. Sponsors fund, and auditors verify configuration.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: On a predictive project, the business analyst produces a formal requirements specification and traceability matrix, while on an agile project the analyst writes user stories in the backlog. Which conclusion does this contrast support?
options: Requirements do not need analysis at all on predictive projects
Agile projects need more upfront documentation than predictive projects
Business analysis is unrelated to the development approach
Elicitation and documentation techniques are shaped by the project's methodology
items.explanation: Methodology influences how business analysis is performed: predictive projects favor formal documentation and baselines, while agile projects capture requirements as backlog stories refined continuously.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst is drafting the inputs needed for an initiative and documents the problem statement, the opportunity, and how success will be measured. Which document set is the analyst primarily preparing inputs for?
options: The business case and benefits management plan
The server configuration checklist
The holiday staffing roster
The marketing slogan list
items.explanation: Needs assessment produces inputs for the business case and benefits management plan, including the problem, opportunity, strategic alignment, and success measures that justify the initiative.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: After a solution goes live, a business analyst measures how the delivered system actually performs against the expected benefits and value defined at the start. Which business analysis activity is being performed?
options: Daily scrum facilitation
Solution evaluation, assessing the delivered solution's performance and value
Requirements elicitation through interviews
Procurement contract closeout
items.explanation: Solution evaluation measures whether the delivered solution meets requirements and achieves the intended business value, enabling go/no-go and course-correction decisions.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: Risk of missed expectations is high for a delivered system, so the business analyst prepares a demonstration and checklist for the customer to confirm that every agreed requirement is satisfied before acceptance. What outcome is the analyst seeking?
options: A request for more suppliers to bid
An approval to delete the traceability records
Formal sign-off validating that the solution meets the agreed requirements
A signed authorization for a budget increase
items.explanation: Validating requirements through product delivery means confirming the solution meets agreed requirements and obtaining formal acceptance, protecting both parties and closing requirement gaps.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: Three candidate architectures could satisfy a business need, and the analyst must choose one using criteria such as cost, scalability, and maintainability with assigned weights. Which evaluation approach should be used?
options: Random selection to keep the process neutral
Selecting the option with the fanciest name
Deferring the choice to the end users only
A multi-criteria decision analysis that scores each option against weighted criteria
items.explanation: Multi-criteria decision analysis systematically scores alternative solutions against weighted criteria, making the choice transparent and aligned with priorities rather than arbitrary.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: While discovering requirements for a payment system, the analyst identifies that regulators impose reporting rules, end users need usability, and the sponsor needs cost control. Which principle has the analyst respected?
options: Requirements can come from many sources, including regulators, users, and sponsors
Only the software developers can supply requirements
Requirements exist solely in the sponsor's budget
Regulators have no influence on requirements
items.explanation: Requirements sources span regulators, customers, sponsors, users, and solution teams; the analyst must identify all relevant sources to capture complete requirements.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A compliance team imposes the rule that all transactions over a threshold must be reported within 24 hours, a constraint the system design must honor. Which element is this rule?
options: A stakeholder satisfaction survey
A business rule that governs and constrains the solution
A user interface color scheme preference
A sprint burndown forecast
items.explanation: Business rules are operating policies or constraints the solution must satisfy, such as regulatory reporting thresholds. Colors, burndown forecasts, and surveys are different artifacts.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst must discover which stakeholders hold the detailed knowledge about inventory rules. The analyst identifies the warehouses and procurement staff as the authoritative sources to interview. Which practice does this reflect?
options: Guessing requirements without speaking to any stakeholders
Waiting until delivery to ask what was needed
Analyzing stakeholders to route elicitation to those who can best supply each requirement
Interviewing all stakeholders for every requirement regardless of relevance
items.explanation: Effective elicitation analyzes stakeholders to determine the right people to involve for each requirement area, tailoring techniques and communication to the audience and the needed information.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: Before eliciting requirements, a business analyst gathers the business case, the problem statement, existing process documentation, and the strategic goals to guide the sessions. Which statement best describes this preparation?
options: Elicitation must begin with no information at all
Elicitation is the same as project closure reporting
Elicitation requires no stakeholder involvement
Elicitation uses inputs such as business documents and as-is artifacts to ask the right questions
items.explanation: Elicitation is grounded in available inputs such as the business case, current process documents, and strategy so questions and techniques are targeted and efficient.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A requirement is written vaguely and cannot be tested, so the analyst rewrites it so it is unambiguous, complete, and measurable. Which quality characteristic of a good requirement is the analyst ensuring?
options: Requirements should be testable, unambiguous, and complete
Requirements should be aspirational and untestable
Requirements should be identical for every stakeholder
Requirements should never change once approved
items.explanation: Well-formed requirements are specific, testable, and complete, so both development and verification can proceed without ambiguity. Untestable or vague statements fail this standard.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A business analyst records for each requirement its identifier, source, priority, status, owner, and associated risk so the set can be managed and traced. Which discipline is being applied?
options: Network performance tuning
Requirements management, maintaining attributes and traceability for each requirement
Project closure archival of final invoices
Marketing campaign analytics
items.explanation: Requirements management captures attributes such as source, priority, status, and owner and maintains traceability so requirements can be analyzed, changed, and verified throughout the project.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: To learn whether a proposed checkout flow works, an agile team builds a small, vertical slice of the flow end to end, ships it to a limited set of users, and measures behavior before expanding. Which concept does this demonstrate?
options: Skipping validation to save effort
Only documenting the flow without building it
Using thin, valuable slices and real feedback to validate the solution progressively
Delivering the entire system with no feedback until the end
items.explanation: Validating requirements progressively through small slices and real user feedback reduces risk and ensures the product converges on genuine value, unlike big-bang delivery and late feedback.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A delivered portal meets its stated requirements, but sales reports show the intended revenue uplift never materialized. The analyst investigates actual usage and benefit realization. Which focus is correct at this stage?
options: Redefining the project charter
Buying more licenses immediately
Closing the stakeholders out of the conversation
Measuring whether the delivered solution achieved the intended business value
items.explanation: Solution evaluation goes beyond requirement compliance to assess whether intended benefits and business value materialized, driving corrective actions such as adoption programs or enhancements.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: After a go-live, the organization tracks benefits and confirms the investment is paying off, and the business analyst captures insights about what worked for future initiatives. Which set of practices is the team completing?
options: Benefits tracking, evaluation, and lessons capture after solution delivery
Daily standup meetings during development
Pre-award contract negotiations
Site selection for the next office
items.explanation: Post-delivery, business analysis verifies benefit realization and collects lessons to improve future work, completing the loop from needs assessment through delivery and evaluation.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks

items.stem: A user requests a significant feature change after signing off on the baseline. Before including it, the analyst documents the requirement, analyzes its full impact, and obtains approval. What must happen before the change is incorporated?
options: The change is noted only verbally at a standup
The change must be evaluated through change control and formally approved
The change is included automatically because a user requested it
The baseline is simply abandoned
items.explanation: Even post-sign-off, changes are incorporated only after impact analysis and formal approval to keep the requirements baseline controlled and deliverables aligned with agreed scope.
items.reference: PMI CAPM Exam Content Outline - Business Analysis Frameworks
